correctness.rationale: For all b>0 and omega>max|b sin u+c sin2u|, polar reduction gives logarithmic radial return I=J(a_*-a). The identity N=-c L is exact. A uniformly convergent even-power expansion of the angular denominator yields signed integrals A_nj=(j-n)/(n+j+1) times a strictly positive beta integral, with the b^2 n=1,j=0 term strictly negative. Hence L<0 globally and the quantitative bound follows. Poisson-kernel Fourier coefficients give a_* prime(0)=q^2 and oddness removes even powers. The fixed-angle radial multiplier proves GAS, global center, or finite escape according to I; integrating dt/dtheta and summing each scaled flight yields the exact T, its critical simple pole and sixth-root radius exponents. The script independently checks 71 finite examples/identities, while the proof is analytical.

value.rationale: Degree seven is the first fourfold-equivariant homogeneous polynomial degree with both angular harmonics 4 and 8 in the radial/angular quotient. The main gap is whether a second harmonic can reverse a seemingly stabilizing radial damping term when angular residence times are coupled to the same Fourier components. A global strict-sign theorem, quantitative lower bound, sharp threshold first derivative, symmetric negative-damping attraction and an exact physical escape clock answer that motivated structural question. The result is nontrivial and not an arbitrary one-parameter numerical slice; it makes no claim to a broad general classification or downstream perturbation theorem.
